findings.reason: mini.js:22 checks `args[0] instanceof Date`, which is false for a Date from another realm (iframe or vm). That Date drops to the else branch at lines 24-31, which applies the localOffset-minus-offset shift, so its timestamp moves. Same-realm Dates are copied as they are. Lowered from medium to low: only Dates built in another realm hit this, and before this change every Date was shifted this way, so nothing regresses.
findings.claim: Date objects from another JavaScript realm skip the new copy branch and get their timestamp shifted by the timezone adjustment.
findings.evidence: The guard uses `args[0] instanceof Date`, which is false for Dates from an iframe or Node vm context. These inputs enter the component-construction branch and receive the localOffset-minus-offset adjustment. A runtime check with TZ=UTC and a vm-created Date at 1707609600000 produced 1707580800000 when passed to `new TZDateMini(input, "Asia/Singapore")`, an eight-hour shift; the same-realm Date preserved its timestamp. TZDate inherits this constructor.
